title: Synchronized Global Inventory Ledger
business: A multinational logistics firm managing real-time stock levels across distributed regional warehouses.
problem: Inconsistent inventory counts caused by network partitions, leading to overselling items that are already allocated to other regions.
solution: Implementing the Raft consensus algorithm to ensure all regional nodes agree on a single, linearizable sequence of inventory updates, preventing conflicting state changes.
steps: Elect a single leader node through a majority vote to coordinate all incoming inventory write requests.
The leader receives an update, appends it to its local log, and replicates the entry to follower nodes.
Follower nodes acknowledge receipt of the log entry, confirming persistence in their local storage.
Once a majority of nodes acknowledge the entry, the leader commits the change and notifies followers to apply it to their state machines.
If a leader fails, followers initiate a new election based on term numbers to restore service.
outcome: A unified, reliable source of truth for inventory levels that remains consistent even if individual nodes or network segments experience temporary failures.
limitation: The primary limitation is latency; because every write requires a round-trip to a majority of nodes, the system performance is constrained by the slowest link in the majority quorum. You can check this by monitoring the time elapsed between a client request and the commit confirmation.

questions.question: In Synchronized Global Inventory Ledger, why is Raft used to solve the inventory problem?
options: To ensure all regional nodes agree on a single, linearizable sequence of inventory updates.
To increase the total number of requests the system can handle per second.
To allow nodes to operate independently without communicating with each other.
To replace the need for network connectivity between regional warehouses.
questions.explanation: Raft provides consensus, which forces distributed nodes to agree on a single order of operations, preventing the conflicts described in the problem.
questions.evidence: Implementing the Raft consensus algorithm to ensure all regional nodes agree on a single, linearizable sequence of inventory updates, preventing conflicting state changes.

questions.question: In Synchronized Global Inventory Ledger, what is a key limitation of the implementation?
options: The system cannot handle more than three nodes.
The system performance is constrained by the slowest link in the majority quorum.
The system requires a manual reset every time a leader is elected.
The system cannot function if a single follower node goes offline.
questions.explanation: Consensus algorithms require a majority quorum, meaning the leader must wait for the majority to respond, making the slowest node in that majority a bottleneck.
questions.evidence: The primary limitation is latency; because every write requires a round-trip to a majority of nodes, the system performance is constrained by the slowest link in the majority quorum.
